subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as a first-run onboarding/auth method, and what scopes, callback, token-storage, refresh, account-detection, billing, and fallback contract should it use?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the OAuth helper and provider auth seams exist, but it cannot choose the product and security contract for presenting Anthropic OAuth as one-click onboarding.

options.title: Approve Additive Provider OAuth
options.body: Expose Anthropic OAuth as an additional provider-owned auth method after security, billing, docs, and live provider proof are accepted.

options.title: Keep Explicit Paths
options.body: Keep API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI as the supported Anthropic setup paths and improve wording or token guidance instead.

options.title: Prototype Behind Experiment
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth flow that does not replace current Anthropic setup choices until provider and security proof is strong.

recommendation.title: Approve Additive Provider OAuth
recommendation.body: Expose Anthropic OAuth as an additional provider-owned auth method after security, billing, docs, and live provider proof are accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal on the Anthropic auth/setup choice surface and recent behavior-shaping review around the related OAuth callback helper.
